capabilities: Clean up wikilinks, embeds, Markdown links, and properties that point at a deleted file
Repoint links to a suggested replacement note, ranked by alias, tags, name, and links
Show a confirmation dialog listing inbound references before deleting a file
Leave plain text or struck-through dated text where a link was removed
Exclude folders such as templates and archives from rewriting
disambiguation: Not a vault-wide broken-link scanner; it only touches links pointing at the file you just deleted.
extras: Not yet in the community plugin directory; manual installation from a GitHub release is described. The README warns that its edits are not undoable with Ctrl+Z and recommends keeping the confirmation dialog on and using version control or Obsidian Sync version history. Property edits go through Obsidian's processFrontMatter, which may normalize YAML quoting and key order.
intentEvidence: When you delete it, the links are left behind, pointing nowhere. This plugin closes that gap
motivation: The author built it because deletion leaves broken links behind, and vault-wide broken-link scanners would wrongly rewrite unresolved links people keep as placeholders.
problem: Obsidian updates links when you rename a note but leaves them dangling when you delete it.
summary: Link cleaner that rewrites, repoints, or leaves plain text in place of links pointing at a file when you delete it.
